report:
### Evidence Summary: Hypnosis for Smoking Cessation

**Conclusion:**
The scientific evidence on whether hypnosis helps with smoking cessation is mixed and inconclusive. Hypnosis may assist certain individuals, particularly when integrated into a broader treatment plan or combined with other cessation strategies, but rigorous systematic reviews show limited and inconsistent evidence that it is consistently effective on its own compared to standard control interventions.

**Key Findings:**
* **Mixed Evidence in Reviews:** Meta-analytic evaluations and systematic reviews (such as Cochrane reviews) analyzing hypnosis for smoking cessation show inconsistent results across clinical trials, with only a few reporting statistically significant effects compared to control conditions (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1330238/full; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6568235).
* **Role in Comprehensive Plans:** Medical resources note that hypnosis is unlikely to be a standalone cure, but it may be useful as part of a larger, multi-faceted program to modify smoking behaviors and manage urges (https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/hypnosis/about/pac-20394405; https://www.healthline.com/health/hypnosis-to-quit-smoking).

### Sources Cited

1. **Mayo Clinic** – Hypnosis Overview: https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/hypnosis/about/pac-20394405
2. **Healthline** – Hypnosis to Quit Smoking: Benefits, Risks, How It Works: https://www.healthline.com/health/hypnosis-to-quit-smoking
3. **Frontiers in Psychology** – Meta-analytic evidence on the efficacy of hypnosis: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1330238/full
4. **PubMed Central (PMC)** – Hypnotherapy for smoking cessation: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6568235
